subject: Archaeology
title: Pompeii: Still Digging After 300 Years
description: A fast breakdown of Pompeii: Still Digging After 300 Years for builders.

hook.text: One-third of Pompeii remains unexcavated after 300 years of digging. Archaeologists are in no hurry to finish.

buildup.text: Modern excavations prioritize preservation over speed. New technology lets teams extract more data from less digging.

discovery.text: In 2020, a well-preserved thermopolium — a Roman fast-food counter — was uncovered with food still in the pots.

twist.text: The unexcavated sections may be better preserved than areas dug up centuries ago and left exposed to weather.

climax.text: Future tools we have not invented yet may reveal things today's technology cannot. Patience is the new strategy.

punchline.text: The best way to preserve Pompeii may be to stop digging it up.

quiz.question: Why are archaeologists leaving parts of Pompeii unexcavated?
options: Funding has run out for further excavation work
Future technology may reveal more than current tools can
The remaining areas are believed to contain nothing significant

details.summary: Pompeii, buried by Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE, has been excavated continuously since 1748 — and a third of the city remains unexcavated. Each decade brings new technology and new discoveries, from fast-food bars to an intact ceremonial chariot, making Pompeii an endlessly revealing archaeological site.
details.whyItMatters: Pompeii is the most detailed snapshot of daily life in any ancient city. Its ongoing excavation shows how archaeology continually reinterprets the past as new methods reveal what earlier diggers missed.
takeaways: Pompeii has been excavated since 1748, over 275 years
About one-third of the city remains unexcavated
New technologies keep revealing previously invisible details

faq.question: Why hasn't all of Pompeii been excavated yet?
faq.answer: Deliberately. Modern archaeologists leave sections buried for future researchers with better technology. Current priorities focus on conserving what's already exposed, which degrades from weather and tourism. Selective excavation also creates research opportunities for applying new methods.

faq.question: What are the most recent discoveries at Pompeii?
faq.answer: Recent finds include a perfectly preserved ceremonial chariot (2021), a fast-food counter (thermopolium) with food still in its serving vessels, and rooms with elaborate frescoes. DNA analysis and CT scanning are revealing new information from remains excavated decades ago.
